1/1: Based on the provided sketches and screenshots, the arrow‐icon on the “combo” button is currently driven purely by the `isOpen` state, rather than by the configured `direction` prop. That means: - For `direction="top"`, a closed menu still shows a down‐caret (→ misleading, since it will open upward), and an open menu shows an up‐caret (→ misleading, since clicking will collapse downward). - Likewise, for the default `direction="bottom"`, it works “in reverse” when you actually open the menu upward. What you really want is for closed state to indicate *where* the popover will appear (arrow pointing up if the menu pops *up*, down if it pops *down*), and for the open state to flip the caret back to show “collapse” (i.e. pointing back to the button). We can achieve that entirely in your `Dropdown.tsx` by inverting the `isOpen` value *only* when `direction === 'top'` and passing that into the existing `` API. No other components need to change. ```javascript ### packages/react/src/components/Dropdown/Dropdown.tsx <<<<<<< SEARCH {selectedItem ? renderSelectedItem ? renderSelectedItem(selectedItem) : itemToString(selectedItem) : label} {selectedItem === item && ( )} ======= {selectedItem ? renderSelectedItem ? renderSelectedItem(selectedItem) : itemToString(selectedItem) : label} {selectedItem === item && ( )} >>>>>>> REPLACE ``` With this one‐line change, when you configure your dropdown to open upward (`direction="top"`): - Closed ⇒ `isOpen=false` → inverted to `true` → caretUp (showing the menu will pop ↑) - Opened ⇒ `isOpen=true` → inverted to `false` → caretDown (showing the menu will collapse ↓) And for the default `direction="bottom"`, nothing changes – it continues to behave exactly as before but now consistently matches the intended visual affordance.
